text:
“I am happy; I am happy to see you here with me; you remembered that I offered you my friendship in an extreme case, and this consoles me for many sorrows.... Ah, I assure you, Loredana, that I am no longer the thoughtless man you once knew! I love you tenderly, and I hope to be able to reassure you....”

She cut off his words with a gesture.

“No,” she replied. “I shall never love you.”

She looked around, and, seeing the glass, raised it to her lips, which she felt were parched by an inward fever.

“Listen to me,” she continued imperiously. “I am here not because I love you, not because I believe in your friendship, but because I wish and must ruin myself.

“Loredana, Loredana, for pity’s sake!” Berto interrupted.

“I must ruin myself. He is about to commit a crime. His ailing mother asked him to abandon me, and he refused.... No, I cannot accept this sacrifice; it is a horrible thing; I must leave him, and in such a way that he will no longer seek me, no longer desire me.... I do not wish to harm his mother, who has already suffered so much because of me.... If she were to die, ah, if she were to die, what remorse, what shame!... And one day he would awaken from this madness; and between him and me, always, always, I would see his mother’s corpse.... I must prevent him from dishonoring himself!”

Berto, standing erect, listened with a sense of wonder to the young woman, who spoke rapidly, agitated by violent excitement; her initial pallor had given way to a feverish flush that crimsoned her cheeks, made her eyes gleam intensely, and reddened her lips, giving them the color of living blood.

He liked her so much thus stretched out in the armchair and sunk into the white fur that Berto bent down once more to kiss her hands. Loredana pushed him away.

“I wanted to kill myself,” she continued, “but it would have been another scandal; perhaps they would have accused Filippo of my death.... Ah, how malicious they all are!... I was told to my face that I am your mistress, that my honor is worth nothing because no one believes me, that a man is a thief when everyone calls him a thief.... How many frightful things I have learned! And then I thought that they were right. The only one who did not doubt me was Filippo; he believes in my love and in my honor, which everyone laughs at; and so he too must cease to believe, so that he may be saved.... I thought that since they call me your mistress, every effort is useless, and I shall never be able to free myself from this accusation....”

“Do not speak like that,” Berto interrupted. “It hurts you too much....”

She stared at him with wide-open eyes; that informal ‘you’ seemed to her more brutal than a kiss that had suddenly sealed her mouth; but Berto noticed and added:

“I beg your pardon; I did not mean to offend you. I love you, and I could not control myself.”

“No,” said Loredana, rising, “let me go!”

Berto dared to lay a hand on her.

“I beg you,” he murmured, “stay a little longer.....”

Loredana shuddered; gathering up the fur, she looked about for her hat. But just as she was about to pick it up again, she stopped as though struck by a thought.

Where was she going? Home, to her own house? Filippo would take her back. To Filippo’s house? His mother would die of it. And by that time Filippo must already have read the few lines Loredana had left him: “I shall never forget you; I shall always love you; the farther away I may seem to you, the more I shall be yours....” And after that, was she to return to him, head bowed, like a repentant schoolgirl, and always too late to be forgiven?

She saw again that accursed half-naked woman with goat’s feet, who, with her right arm raised, seemed to command her to stop. She turned, and on the other side saw Berto, who did not dare move to hold her back, did not dare speak for fear of frightening her, and kept watching her, trying to divine from her gestures the decision she would make.

She returned to her armchair, let herself fall into it, and said not a word.

Thus followed an anguished silence of several minutes, during which Loredana and Berto stared keenly at each other, motionless, as though scrutinizing one another; but Berto could endure it no longer, approached her again, and seized her hands.

“Stay!” he said, his voice veiled with passion. “Stay! I implore you! I know you do not love me, and that does not frighten me....”

He was trying to remove one of her gloves; she noticed and unbuttoned it with a swift gesture, offering him her bare hand and wrist to kiss; but when she felt those avid lips upon her flesh, she turned her head away, almost in revulsion.

“No!” she said. “Wait!”

She seized the glass and drained it avidly, then held it out to Berto again so that he might pour more, and drank again; but, catching sight of herself in the mirror, she threw the empty glass to the floor, where it shattered.

“What do you wish to do with me?” she then said.

“Anything you command me to do,” Berto replied. “I am free; I can leave today, tonight, tomorrow, whenever you ask me.”

“Yes,” Loredana declared. “We shall leave at once. We shall go to Rome.”

She burst into such harsh, sardonic laughter that Berto looked at her in fear.

“To Rome,” Loredana repeated. “I was to go there with Flopi; I shall go with you. Is it not the same? Am I not your mistress? Did they not want me to be your mistress? One man or another, it matters little.... Why do we not go to Sirmione as well?... I wish to trample upon all my past, I wish to destroy every memory, I wish nothing to remain, nothing at all of what was so dear to me, and what would make me blush!... Ah, you do not know the horror I feel for life!... You think only of taking possession of me; I see it in your eyes, and you do not understand that I am no longer alive, you do not understand that I hate you, and the closer you come to me, the more I hate you!...”

Berto did not reply, but the hand that held the young woman’s relaxed its grip; he drew back, stricken by the savage vehemence of those words.

“Why do you want me?” Loredana continued, casting him a contemptuous glance. “I love Filippo, and I am sacrificing myself for him. Is that not clear? Is it not clear that I wish to ruin myself in order to save him? Have I not already told you! And I chose you of all people so that he will despise me so much that he will no longer seek me!... And you lend yourself to this game?... If I consented to become your mistress, that would be the moment when I loved Filippo most, because that would be the gravest sacrifice I could make for him.... And you did not understand that? How must I tell you that I shall never love you?”
